Hello! I am Daniel, a first-year math student at AUB. I am currently working on formalizing the following theorem (which could hopefully be a part of mathlib eventually): given two Hermitian matrices A and B that commute, they must be both simultaneously diagonalizable.

However, in proving this statement, I ran into the following issue: for example, say we have matrices A (2 by 2), B (3 by 3), C (1 by 1), and I want to construct a matrix of the following form: 

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│    A    │    0    │      0      │
│  (2×2)  │         │             │
│─────────────────────────────────│
│    0    │    B    │      0      │
│         │  (3×3)  │             │
│─────────────────────────────────│
│    0    │    0    │      C      │
│         │         │    (1×1)    │
└─────────────────────────────────┘

Of course the names and dimensions of the matrices are arbitrary and I chose these specifically purely for the sake of clarity.
Is there a function or definition of some kind that is able to achieve this?

Now, there is Matrix.diagonal d in mathlib, which gives us a matrix with the vector d along the diagonal. However, what I am looking for is something similar to this but, instead of a vector along the diagonal, I want these matrices (preferably arbitrarily many such matrices) to be placed as blocks along the diagonal.

Thanks for your help!

Eric Wieser said:

This is docs#Matrix.blockDiagonal'

Thank you!
As a warmup and an opportunity to contribute to mathlib, you could prove that a block diagonal matrix of hermitian matrices is itself hermitian
:shrug: nothing found

Eric Wieser said:

you could prove that a block diagonal matrix of hermitian matrices is itself hermitian

Do you need the matrix to be block-diagonal? Isn't it true for arbitrary block-hermitian matrices?
I guess one doesn't need the blocks to be hermitian away from the diagonal

Yaël Dillies said:

I guess one doesn't need the blocks to be hermitian away from the diagonal

Yes, but I mean this is not a terribly big deal, since the matrix M would be of the form: 

┌──────────────┐
│  A   │   B   │
│──────────────│
│  C   │   D   │
└──────────────┘

For M = M*, we need A = A*, D = D*, and B = C*. Both A = A* and D = D* I have proven already for the block-diagonal case, and since it's block-diagonal, B = C* was trivially satisfied. It is true though that we do not need to require that and we only need B = C* for the proof to hold more generally.

In working with fromBlocks, which I originally wanted to use to prove this (at least intuitively) more specific case, I found that it only handles a 2-block structure (2 by 2), while blockDiagonal' is indexed by an arbitrary type o. So, I think there's no way to reduce a general blockDiagonal' to fromBlocks unless o has exactly two elements. Is it okay if my proof of this theorem will not rely on fromBlocks and will be built independently, but with a similar approach?
Hello! I opened a PR for this: #37933. Thanks for your help!

Nice!

when I tried reviewing it I ended up golfing it a lot

Spoiler

theorem isHermitian_blockDiagonal'_iff {o : Type*} [DecidableEq o] {blockSize : o → Type*}
    (M : ∀ i : o, Matrix (blockSize i) (blockSize i) α) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' M).IsHermitian ↔ ∀ i, (M i).IsHermitian := by
  grind [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.blockDiagonal'_conjTranspose, Matrix.blockDiagonal'_inj]
